codes.Label: Intermittent functioning / drops mid-task
codes.Note: Works, then abruptly stops within a session.

codes.Label: Wi-Fi dependency / network switching
codes.Note: Tied to Wi-Fi. Breaks across venues. Reluctance to change network settings.

codes.Label: Cold-start warm-up ritual
codes.Note: Primes the device with music first to confirm the connection.

codes.Label: No resume after a drop
codes.Note: Restarts a task from the beginning after a failure.

codes.Label: Wake-word non-response
codes.Note: Wake word repeated many times. Question cut off. Restart.

codes.Label: Battery life limits
codes.Note: Short runtime. Continuous modes drain faster.

codes.Label: Hardware, version, operating system dependency
codes.Note: Behavior tied to phone and glasses generation, plus operating system version.

codes.Label: Live AI response lag
codes.Note: Continuous mode describes what was there seconds ago. Stale for walking and moving scenes.

codes.Label: Update regression
codes.Note: A software update made a working feature slower or worse.

codes.Label: No offline mode
codes.Note: Core features need a live connection. Off the grid the device stops working.

codes.Label: Bluetooth and audio handoff failure
codes.Note: Audio route drops or defaults back to the phone mid-use.

codes.Label: Idle sleep state
codes.Note: Device sleeps when idle. First command after idle is lost.

codes.Label: Answers from the previous frame
codes.Note: Returns the last image's content when the connection flickers. No signal that the frame is old.

codes.Label: Time to connect before the task
codes.Note: Putting them on, waiting for pairing, waiting for a call to land. Often longer than doing it another way.
codes.Sub-theme: Time to connect before the task

codes.Label: Refuses on a state that is not true
codes.Note: Says it cannot act because the user is on a call when no call is running.
codes.Sub-theme: Refuses on a state that is not true

codes.Label: Head movement disconnects the device
codes.Note: Bending or looking down drops the connection and stops audio mid-task. Resets rather than resumes.

codes.Label: Reading labels / mail / documents (success)
codes.Note: Reads printed labels, mail, ingredient lists, documents. Works.

codes.Label: Number-reading errors
codes.Note: Misreads digits. Scrambles numbers in rows. Single numbers fine.

codes.Label: Currency identification unreliable
codes.Note: Bill and denomination recognition inconsistent. Needs a fallback.

codes.Label: Summary instead of full read, silent omission
codes.Note: Summarizes on its own. Omits needed content unless told to read all.
codes.Sub-theme: Summary instead of full read, silent omission

codes.Label: Handwriting recognition weak
codes.Note: Handwritten text read with low, variable accuracy.

codes.Label: Reading digital screens
codes.Note: Reading content on phone, computer, appliance, TV screens.

codes.Label: Full book and multi-page reading (success)
codes.Note: Reads both facing pages in order, any orientation. Page turn by one button press.

codes.Label: Real-time capture coaching (success)
codes.Note: Spoken framing coaching. Move closer, turn to the light, stay still, got it.

codes.Label: Aiming and re-framing burden
codes.Note: User cannot see where the camera points. Partial reads blamed on own head angle.

codes.Label: Complex layout parsing failure
codes.Note: Long single-page or multi-column layouts read out of order or mismatched.

codes.Label: Numerals read without meaning
codes.Note: Reads a figure but cannot tell a temperature from a clock time.

codes.Label: Menu reading in venues
codes.Note: Restaurant, coffee bar, buffet menus. Recurs across every participant.

codes.Label: Reads a control it cannot operate
codes.Note: Names an on-screen button the user still cannot reach or press.
codes.Sub-theme: Reads a control it cannot operate

codes.Label: Editorial commentary
codes.Note: Adds praise or judgement to a document read. Tolerated while brief.
codes.Sub-theme: Unrequested opinion added to a reading

codes.Label: Capturing content that is up briefly
codes.Note: Shared agenda on a call, up for 30 seconds. Grab and read.
codes.Sub-theme: Capturing on-screen content that is up briefly

codes.Label: Says why it cannot read
codes.Note: Names the blocker: too small, too blurry, not enough light. Reports conflict on whether it does this.

codes.Label: Glare and lamination defeat reading
codes.Note: Laminated menus and window glass. Reads only the big words.

codes.Label: No handoff to the phone
codes.Note: Wants the captured text in the app as a notification. Read it again, save it, braille it.
codes.Sub-theme: No handoff of the text to the phone

codes.Label: No jumping to a section
codes.Note: Take me to the soups. No structure to move around in.

codes.Label: Output gone once spoken
codes.Note: No way back into what was just read. Audio only, one pass.

codes.Label: Summary on purpose
codes.Note: Long letters, deliberately summarised. Opposite of the silent omission complaint.

codes.Label: Refuses to read on policy grounds
codes.Note: Declines named material rather than reporting a capture problem. Copyright is the usual trigger.
codes.Sub-theme: Refuses to read on policy grounds

codes.Label: Asking about one region of a page
codes.Note: Isolating a row, a line or a gauge reading. Fingers used as a physical crop.
codes.Sub-theme: Asking about one region of a page

codes.Label: Live screens versus a still capture
codes.Note: A refreshing display and a single frame do not line up.
codes.Sub-theme: Live screens versus a still capture

codes.Label: Medication and dosage labels
codes.Note: High-stakes label reading. Curved bottles, small print, rotation needed.

codes.Label: Multi-frame scan mode wanted
codes.Note: Keep the page in frame, take several shots, assemble one reading.

codes.Label: On-device QR and code scanning
codes.Note: Scans a code and pushes the link to the phone. Little spoken feedback.

codes.Label: Habitual gaze direction misaims the camera
codes.Note: Residual peripheral vision pulls the head off the normative sightline, so the camera captures the wrong thing.
codes.Sub-theme: Habitual gaze direction misaims the camera

codes.Label: Coaching the user cannot act on
codes.Note: Tells the user to flatten, move or reposition in ways their vision or the object will not allow.
codes.Sub-theme: Coaching the user cannot act on

codes.Label: Cannot tell which on-screen item is selected
codes.Note: Reads the menu items and leaves the highlight unreported, so the user counts positions instead.
codes.Sub-theme: Cannot tell which on-screen item is selected

codes.Label: Scene / room description (success)
codes.Note: Describes surroundings, layout, objects in view. Works.

codes.Label: Color identification / matching
codes.Note: Naming colors for clothing matching and outfit checks.

codes.Label: Low-light degradation + feedback
codes.Note: Accuracy drops in poor light and glare. Device flags the limit.

codes.Label: Description limits (specifics)
codes.Note: Won't name ambiguous items or substances. Generic description only.

codes.Label: Condition / cleanliness judgment limits
codes.Note: Won't reliably judge state such as clean, empty, full, done.

codes.Label: Finding dropped / misplaced objects
codes.Note: Directional cues for dropped or misplaced items.

codes.Label: Off-frame content missed
codes.Note: Single-frame capture misses objects outside the view.

codes.Label: Background clutter in the description
codes.Note: Reads everything in frame including background. User has to sort signal from noise.

codes.Label: Prompt specificity burden
codes.Note: Only a precisely scoped question returns the wanted item.

codes.Label: No detail-level control
codes.Note: No way to ask for shorter or longer. Detail costs time in live settings.

codes.Label: Store shelf and product search
codes.Note: Aisle, shelf, product and brand location in shops.

codes.Label: Art and image description
codes.Note: Museums, gallery labels, graffiti. Framed as audio description for still images.

codes.Label: Appliance state verification
codes.Note: Reads knob settings and displays to confirm the user set it right.

codes.Label: Description from a moving vehicle
codes.Note: Live description of roadside scene at speed. Lag makes it stale.

codes.Label: Live event and sports description
codes.Note: Racetrack, grandstand, leaderboard. Named as the top future use.

codes.Label: Photo capture and framing
codes.Note: Taking photos, aiming, no way to confirm the shot before sending.

codes.Label: Content policy blocks description
codes.Note: Refuses to name characters or judge food doneness. Copyright and liability limits.

codes.Label: Cannot find visual affordances
codes.Note: Signs, QR menus and cues exist but the user does not know to look for them.

codes.Label: Describes a saved photo
codes.Note: Ask AI on a shot in the gallery. Only shots taken with the glasses.

codes.Label: Orientation not flagged
codes.Note: Does not say the page or item is upside down. Reports conflict.
codes.Sub-theme: Orientation of the item not flagged

codes.Label: Curved and round packaging fails
codes.Note: Bowls, cans and bottles defeat the capture where flat boxes succeed.

codes.Label: Cannot magnify or reach further
codes.Note: No zoom. Anything beyond arm's length is described, never enlarged.

codes.Label: Says no and stops there
codes.Note: Answers the yes-or-no question without offering what it does see.

codes.Label: Set, stage and venue description thin
codes.Note: Generic answers where the detail is the whole point.
codes.Sub-theme: Set, stage and venue description thin

codes.Label: Blinking or changing indicators not reported
codes.Note: A single frame cannot carry a flashing light, a moving needle or an alternating panel.
codes.Sub-theme: Blinking or changing indicators not reported

codes.Label: Culturally specific items misidentified
codes.Note: Foods and objects outside the training distribution get generic or wrong names.

codes.Label: Appearance / expression description (success)
codes.Note: Describes appearance, posture, emotion, and surroundings. Works.

codes.Label: No face recognition / enrollment (wish)
codes.Note: No enrollment or recognition of known individuals. Stated request.

codes.Label: Person-locating wish (spatial)
codes.Note: Wants to locate a specific person in space or take a roll call of a room.

codes.Label: Background noise breaks interaction
codes.Note: Crowds, chatter, music block command recognition.

codes.Label: Social stigma / recording perception
codes.Note: Conspicuous device draws scrutiny. Bystanders wary of recording.

codes.Label: Voice commands awkward in public
codes.Note: Speaking commands aloud draws attention. Whisper or skip it.
codes.Sub-theme: Voice commands awkward in public / quiet settings

codes.Label: Race, gender and age estimates
codes.Note: Values a best guess at ethnicity, gender, age. Frames it as equal access to what sighted people see.

codes.Label: Vendor policy limits person description
codes.Note: Some devices refuse to name or classify people. Users read this as withheld information.

codes.Label: Mainstream appeal lowers stigma
codes.Note: Sighted buyers make the device ordinary. Bystanders read it as a gadget.

codes.Label: Bans and hostility
codes.Note: Businesses barring the glasses. Reports of pairs smashed. Risk to a device used as an accommodation.

codes.Label: Fails in front of an audience
codes.Note: Showing it off, it invents an answer. Social cost on top of the task cost.
codes.Sub-theme: Fails in front of an audience

codes.Label: People do the wayfinding
codes.Note: Friends announce their names. Staff and waiters seat and steer.
codes.Sub-theme: People around the user do the wayfinding

codes.Label: Onlookers moved
codes.Note: Family friends cry at a face description. User unmoved.
codes.Sub-theme: Sighted onlookers moved by the demo

codes.Label: Partial sight read as none
codes.Note: No white cane, so no disability read. Fifty percent sight not understood.
codes.Sub-theme: Partial sight read as no disability

codes.Label: Family refuses to be enrolled
codes.Note: The people around the user veto face training, so the feature never gets tested.

codes.Label: Enrollment from a roster or contact list
codes.Note: Class list, contact photos, an existing photo library as the enrollment source.
codes.Sub-theme: Enrollment from a roster or contact list

codes.Label: Facial expression and social cues
codes.Note: Eye rolls, reactions, who just walked in. Invisible to the user by default.

codes.Label: Gender guessing carries social risk
codes.Note: A wrong pronoun read from appearance has a social cost the user then carries.

codes.Label: Read as a shoplifter while using it
codes.Note: Standing with a product long enough to scan it looks like theft, so use is confined to stores where staff know the user.
codes.Sub-theme: Read as a shoplifter while using it

codes.Label: Announces the device to preempt suspicion
codes.Note: Pre-emptive explanation to staff and bystanders as the price of using it in public.
codes.Sub-theme: Announces the device to preempt suspicion

codes.Label: Glasses read as sight by bystanders
codes.Note: Wearing them makes people treat the user as sighted, so gestures and signals go unanswered.
codes.Sub-theme: Glasses read as sight by bystanders

codes.Label: Greeting rules raise the cost of not recognising people
codes.Note: Cultural etiquette requires naming each relative on entry, so failure to recognise reads as rudeness.
codes.Sub-theme: Greeting rules raise the cost of not recognising people

codes.Label: Reassurance offered instead of information
codes.Note: Sighted people answer with it is fine rather than with the fact asked for.

codes.Label: Missed handshakes and waves read as rudeness
codes.Note: Field loss means outstretched hands and high-fives go unseen, and the social penalty lands on the user.
codes.Sub-theme: Missed handshakes and waves read as rudeness

codes.Label: Challenged in public over the device as a recorder
codes.Note: Ushers, staff or students demand an account of the glasses while they are being used for access.
codes.Sub-theme: Challenged in public over the device as a recorder

codes.Label: Live demonstration during the session succeeds
codes.Note: Participant runs the device on camera during the interview and the exchange is captured verbatim.
codes.Sub-theme: Live demonstration during the session succeeds

codes.Label: Wake-word friction
codes.Note: Every command needs the wake word. Wake word not user-changeable.

codes.Label: Rapid-sequence conversation works
codes.Note: Fast follow-ups sustain a conversation. 'Continue' and 'read more' extend replies.

codes.Label: No conversation memory / continuity (wish)
codes.Note: No resume of a prior session. Wants a continue-last-conversation prompt.

codes.Label: Live AI continuous mode
codes.Note: Hands-free continuous mode. Kills repeated wake word. Costs battery.

codes.Label: Gesture / alt activation (wish)
codes.Note: Interest in non-voice activation. Voice still required to start.

codes.Label: Command must be complete and precise
codes.Note: Partial phrasing gets a partial action. Photo taken, no description.
codes.Sub-theme: Command must be complete and precise

codes.Label: Listening-state confirmation
codes.Note: Users listen for the beep to know it heard them. Missing the beep costs a retry.

codes.Label: No speaker recognition
codes.Note: Any voice in the room interrupts. Device cannot tell the wearer from bystanders.

codes.Label: Captured frame retained for follow-ups
codes.Note: Holds one shot in memory so the user can look away and still ask about it.

codes.Label: Physical button and touchpad control (success)
codes.Note: Silent mode switching and page turns. Works in libraries and quiet rooms.

codes.Label: Too many functions on one button
codes.Note: Up to six click counts on one control. Users lose count.
codes.Sub-theme: Too many functions on one button

codes.Label: Dictation and message composition
codes.Note: Speech to text for messages. Rated more reliable than the phone assistant.

codes.Label: No in-place edit of dictated text
codes.Note: Only cancel and restart. No replace this sentence.
codes.Sub-theme: No in-place edit of dictated text

codes.Label: Pointing as a frame cue
codes.Note: Hand or finger used to narrow what the camera should answer about.

codes.Label: Proactive alerting (wish)
codes.Note: Wants a standing watch for a target: this gate, this aisle, this hazard.

codes.Label: Audio output competes with the room
codes.Note: Output volume needed to hear it drowns out the live conversation.
codes.Sub-theme: Audio output competes with the room

codes.Label: Non-native English recognition friction
codes.Note: Speaker translates in their head first. Device misses the request.

codes.Label: Live translation feature
codes.Note: Translates a speaker into the user's language. Talks over the live voice.

codes.Label: Do not disturb respected
codes.Note: Phone on silent, messages not read aloud. Works, and is valued.

codes.Label: Wording is the work
codes.Note: Half the job is finding the phrasing. No guidance on what phrasing wins.
codes.Sub-theme: Getting the wording right is the work

codes.Label: Assistant acts like a friend
codes.Note: Conversational padding where a tool answer was wanted. Named as a reason to downgrade.

codes.Label: Accessibility detail setting found
codes.Note: A setting that lengthens descriptions for blind users. Discovered, not offered.

codes.Label: Answers as if the user can see
codes.Note: Deictic and visual phrasing, right in front of you, this one, with no non-visual anchor.
codes.Sub-theme: Answers as if the user can see

codes.Label: Same words route to the wrong capability
codes.Note: A read or colour request returns a scene description. The words register while the intent behind them is missed.
codes.Sub-theme: Same words route to the wrong capability

codes.Label: Wants instructions one step at a time
codes.Note: The whole list at once is unusable while the hands are busy. Asked for by three participants.
codes.Sub-theme: Wants instructions one step at a time

codes.Label: Notifications interrupt media playback
codes.Note: Message announcements cut across podcasts and audiobooks, and the setting is not findable.

codes.Label: Offers an action nobody asked for
codes.Note: Proposes calls and messages unprompted, then apologises when corrected.
codes.Sub-theme: Offers an action nobody asked for

codes.Label: Wants sound identification and direction
codes.Note: Asks the device to name and place a sound rather than only what the camera sees.

codes.Label: Glasses blocked by app phone
codes.Note: Glasses inoperable while the app's host phone is in use.
codes.Sub-theme: Cannot use glasses while app-phone is active

codes.Label: Blocks core workflows
codes.Note: Conflict blocks reading notes or a book during calls and meetings.

codes.Label: Second-phone workaround
codes.Note: Second phone, no app on it, used to read during a call.

codes.Label: Phone seizes the audio route
codes.Note: Call or meeting audio jumps between phone and glasses without the user choosing.

codes.Label: One paired device at a time
codes.Note: Bound to the phone, so not available for the tablet. Headsets pair to two.
codes.Sub-theme: One paired device at a time

codes.Label: Fallback to human / other services
codes.Note: Handoff to Be My Eyes, Aira, Seeing AI, sighted person on failure or high stakes.

codes.Label: Screen reader primary for phone
codes.Note: On-phone and banking reading stays with the screen reader.
codes.Sub-theme: Screen reader / VoiceOver primary for phone content

codes.Label: ChatGPT everyday use
codes.Note: Daily use of a general chatbot as a personal assistant and reference.

codes.Label: Hands-free = unique value
codes.Note: Hands-free operation at eye level. The key differentiator.

codes.Label: Missing apps and AI on device
codes.Note: Wants other assistants, points-of-interest search, maps, third-party apps on the glasses.
codes.Sub-theme: Missing apps and AI on device

codes.Label: Messaging platform limits
codes.Note: Only first-party messaging. No WhatsApp or Signal. Contact-based photo sending works well.

codes.Label: Glasses replace headphones
codes.Note: Music, audiobooks, calls. Displaced earbuds entirely for some.

codes.Label: Everyday assistant utilities
codes.Note: Timers, reminders, weather, hours, location, calls, texts, photos.

codes.Label: Phone assistant passthrough
codes.Note: Phone assistant answers through the glasses. Users cannot tell which system replied.

codes.Label: Explicit tool-to-tool comparison
codes.Note: Users rate the glasses against Seeing AI, Be My Eyes, Aira, other glasses.

codes.Label: Looks it up online instead
codes.Note: Googles the menu or the fact rather than fight the camera.

codes.Label: One AI supports the other
codes.Note: Chatbot walked the user through a hard reset. Saved a return.
codes.Sub-theme: One AI used to troubleshoot the other

codes.Label: Braille controller alongside
codes.Note: Pocket keyboard drives the phone, glasses carry the audio. Phone never comes out.
codes.Sub-theme: Braille or physical controller paired alongside

codes.Label: Closed camera
codes.Note: Promised developer kit not shipped. Camera locked to one vendor's AI.

codes.Label: Integration never set up
codes.Note: Knows the integration exists. Never got it working. No clear path from either app.

codes.Label: Earlier glasses as benchmark
codes.Note: Aira wireless glasses, 2017. Bulky, one function. Todays hardware measured against it.
codes.Sub-theme: Earlier smart glasses as the benchmark

codes.Label: Long messages truncated
codes.Note: Reads two or three sentences, then sends the user to the phone.

codes.Label: Literal reader trusted more
codes.Note: Seeing AI reads what is there and fails visibly. The glasses fail fluently.
codes.Sub-theme: Literal reader trusted over generative describer

codes.Label: On-ramp to other services
codes.Note: Bought the glasses, then finally started using the volunteer service.
codes.Sub-theme: Glasses as the on-ramp to other services

codes.Label: Smart home stack
codes.Note: Voice lights, motorised blinds, app-run washer, smart microwave. Replaces the reading task.

codes.Label: Toolkit thinking
codes.Note: No one way fits all. Users hold five or six tools and pick per task.
codes.Sub-theme: Toolkit thinking, no single tool wins

codes.Label: Reluctance to call a volunteer
codes.Note: Nervous about who answers. Does not want to spend a stranger's time. Paid agents feel safer.
codes.Sub-theme: Reluctance to call a human volunteer

codes.Label: Desktop assistive technology as the baseline
codes.Note: CCTV magnifier, universal reader, screen magnification. The glasses are measured against these.
codes.Sub-theme: Desktop assistive technology as the baseline

codes.Label: Third-party continuous narration app
codes.Note: A separate app that keeps describing without a prompt.

codes.Label: AI drafts the writing
codes.Note: Email, scripts, descriptions. Drafted by a chatbot, then edited by hand.

codes.Label: Dedicated single-purpose device
codes.Note: A standalone bill reader kept because it is faster and certain.

codes.Label: Open ear keeps ambient hearing available
codes.Note: Named as the single favourite property. Earbuds close off the room. The glasses leave it open.
codes.Sub-theme: Open ear keeps ambient hearing available

codes.Label: Knowledge queries with no camera involved
codes.Note: Prices, comparisons, facts and hours asked of the assistant with nothing in frame.
codes.Sub-theme: Knowledge queries with no camera involved

codes.Label: Glasses back up a failing screen reader
codes.Note: When VoiceOver will not read the message, the glasses read the phone screen instead.
codes.Sub-theme: Glasses back up a failing screen reader

codes.Label: Purchase channel determines support
codes.Note: Where it was bought shapes setup help and returns.

codes.Label: Customer support broken
codes.Note: Support channel unresponsive. Text only.

codes.Label: Onboarding / tutorial ease
codes.Note: App-guided setup and tutorial. Self-service worked.

codes.Label: Community / facilitator learning
codes.Note: Peer and facilitator instruction drives adoption.

codes.Label: Vendor feedback loop works
codes.Note: In-device bug reports, known-issue lists, users treated as testers.

codes.Label: Wants training, unsure of capability
codes.Note: Owns the device, does not know what it can do. Asks the researchers to teach them.

codes.Label: Blind people on the design staff
codes.Note: Users cite blind staff as the reason features fit. Drives brand trust.
codes.Sub-theme: Blind people on the design staff

codes.Label: Clinician or professional referral
codes.Note: Heard about the device from an eye doctor or a rehabilitation contact.

codes.Label: Settings re-enabled for every pair
codes.Note: Owning two identical pairs means setting everything up twice.

codes.Label: Device arrived as a gift
codes.Note: Given by someone in the user's community, which also decides how much training came with it.

codes.Label: Outside the peer channel
codes.Note: Not in the forums or groups. One friend is the entire information source about the device.

codes.Label: How-to content aimed at sighted users
codes.Note: Available tutorials teach travel vlogging and covert recording. Non-visual use is absent from them.
codes.Sub-theme: How-to content aimed at sighted users

codes.Label: No accessible record of what changed
codes.Note: Capabilities appear and disappear between updates with no announcement the user can find.
codes.Sub-theme: No accessible record of what changed

codes.Label: Low personal privacy concern
codes.Note: Little worry about the device observing private space. Several say they should worry more.

codes.Label: Bystander privacy awareness
codes.Note: Aware of covert capture and misuse. Asks permission before posting.

codes.Label: Auto-redaction of sensitive info
codes.Note: Device declines to read certain sensitive items.

codes.Label: Deliberate withholding from AI
codes.Note: Users self-censor. No client data, no bank statements, no benefit letters.

codes.Label: Capture storage and deletion
codes.Note: Description shots are saved. Users manage transfer and deletion by hand.

codes.Label: Recording indicator meaning
codes.Note: Indicator light unreadable to bystanders and switchable off.

codes.Label: Platform policy shapes features
codes.Note: Users track platform privacy policy changes and expect feature changes to follow.

codes.Label: Unclear data-use consent
codes.Note: Cannot recall whether they opted in to data use. No visible control after setup.

codes.Label: Ad targeting
codes.Note: Live conversation feeding ads. Suspicion that place recommendations are paid.
codes.Sub-theme: Ad targeting from what it sees and hears

codes.Label: Strip bystanders from captures
codes.Note: Plates, house numbers, neighbours' children in a posted video. Currently a sighted spouse checks.
codes.Sub-theme: Wants bystander data stripped from captures

codes.Label: Threat is financial
codes.Note: Prior identity theft. Bank statements withheld. Location tracking shrugged off.
codes.Sub-theme: Named threat is financial, not surveillance

codes.Label: Tolerance tracks usefulness
codes.Note: Accurate enough and the data cost stops mattering. Inaccurate and it is theft for nothing.

codes.Label: Trust differs by vendor
codes.Note: Same data, different company, different comfort. Social platform ownership is the concern.

codes.Label: Will not use it in private spaces
codes.Note: Bathrooms, changing rooms. The wearer polices the camera on everyone else's behalf.
codes.Sub-theme: Will not use it in private spaces

codes.Label: Wants processing kept on device
codes.Note: Face data and images held locally as the condition for using the feature.

codes.Label: Content acceptable, identifier withheld
codes.Note: Willing to have the instructions read, unwilling to have the name on the label captured.

codes.Label: Protects another person's information
codes.Note: Chooses the AI over a human volunteer to keep a relative's medical data out of a stranger's view.

codes.Label: Lowers the volume so bystanders cannot hear
codes.Note: The privacy risk named is the spoken output rather than the captured image.
codes.Sub-theme: Lowers the volume so bystanders cannot hear

codes.Label: Believes the data stays local
codes.Note: Assumes the loop is the glasses and the phone only, and revises that belief when asked.

codes.Label: Independence & dignity
codes.Note: Self-reliant acts that used to need a sighted helper or a staff member.

codes.Label: Novel / creative uses
codes.Note: Inventive uses beyond the interview guide.

codes.Label: Learning (languages, hair, hobbies)
codes.Note: Device as a learning aid.

codes.Label: Companionship / conversation partner
codes.Note: Social and conversational use of the AI.

codes.Label: Hobby and special-interest deep use
codes.Note: Records, art, motorsport. Long multi-turn sessions in one domain.

codes.Label: Self-presentation and appearance feedback
codes.Note: How do I look. Outfit, hair, makeup. Currently unmet and mostly unasked.

codes.Label: Closes a previously closed experience
codes.Note: Any book off any shelf. A leaderboard. A painting. A handout in class.

codes.Label: Sport and outdoor recreation
codes.Note: Kayaking, tennis, cycling. Timing cues and hazard calls rather than description.

codes.Label: Playing an inaccessible video game
codes.Note: A mainstream game made playable by a person looking through the camera.

codes.Label: Names information sighted people get by default
codes.Note: Frames the request as access to what everyone else already has rather than as a special feature.
codes.Sub-theme: Names information sighted people get by default

codes.Label: Label access changes a health decision
codes.Note: Reading sugar and ingredient content in the aisle changes what gets bought.
codes.Sub-theme: Label access changes a health decision

codes.Label: Following a live instructor
codes.Note: Wants a group exercise class called out as it happens when the teacher does not cue verbally.

codes.Label: Driving named as the wish
codes.Note: Asked what a magical version would do, the answer is drive.

codes.Label: Animal care tasks
codes.Note: Finding waste, vomit and sores on an animal. Unglamorous, frequent, and unserved.

codes.Label: Frame sizing and slippage
codes.Note: One size fits all. Smallest frame still too wide. Slides down the nose.

codes.Label: Weight and bulk
codes.Note: Frames heavy and thick. A reason to leave them off.

codes.Label: Prescription lens support
codes.Note: Prescription gates purchase. Long-distance script blocks reading work. Second pair breaks the glasses.

codes.Label: Tint and transition lenses
codes.Note: Sunglasses bonus for light sensitivity. Also darkens an already dark visual field.

codes.Label: Charging case as power bank
codes.Note: Case recharges the glasses about twice in the field. Named as the top hardware advantage.

codes.Label: Obtrusive audible alerts
codes.Note: Case beep too loud for a library or a meeting.

codes.Label: Control placement and handedness
codes.Note: Touchpad on the cane-hand side. No left or right option.

codes.Label: Physical control layout
codes.Note: Volume, touchpad, companion app settings. Works when discoverable.

codes.Label: Lens fogging and kitchen conditions
codes.Note: Steam and vapour blur the lenses during cooking.

codes.Label: Outward camera blocks self-view
codes.Note: Cannot point it at yourself. Mirror is the only workaround.

codes.Label: Microphone pickup profile
codes.Note: Isolates the wearer for video but not for live AI. Inconsistent noise handling.

codes.Label: Aesthetics and colour choice
codes.Note: Looks matter. Users want size and colour options, not one look.

codes.Label: Output cannot beat the street
codes.Note: No noise cancelling. Cupped hand as the workaround. Loud venues rule it out.
codes.Sub-theme: Open ear output cannot beat the street

codes.Label: Camera below phone quality
codes.Note: Grainy for volunteers. Visibly worse than the phone at the same scene.

codes.Label: Pressure on the eyes and face
codes.Note: The weight sits on the face all day and becomes a reason to take them off.
codes.Sub-theme: Pressure on the eyes and face

codes.Label: Fragility and breakage risk
codes.Note: Walking into a wall breaks them. No safety-glass build.

codes.Label: Not water resistant
codes.Note: Rules out water sports and rain.

codes.Label: Case charge state is visual only
codes.Note: Charge and pairing state shown by a coloured light the wearer cannot see.
codes.Sub-theme: Case charge state is visual only

codes.Label: Lenses chosen for eye protection
codes.Note: Polycarbonate on medical advice, because the wearer walks into things.

codes.Label: Wants an in-lens visual overlay
codes.Note: A participant with usable central vision wants the answer drawn on the world rather than spoken.

codes.Label: Did not know it could do that
codes.Note: Feature exists, never tried. Often discovered during the interview.
codes.Sub-theme: Did not know it could do that

codes.Label: Hesitancy and AI shyness
codes.Note: Intimidated by conversational AI. Self-describes as a little AI shy.

codes.Label: Forgets to wear or carry
codes.Note: Left at home, then wished for outside. The most common reported blocker.

codes.Label: Battery anxiety suppresses outings
codes.Note: Leaves them behind because the charge might not last.

codes.Label: Human helper substitutes
codes.Note: Paid aide, spouse, daughter, friend already does the task.

codes.Label: Existing tactile or memory system works
codes.Note: Braille labels, tactile marks, fixed order, known layout.
codes.Sub-theme: Existing tactile or memory system works

codes.Label: Mobility limits reduce out-of-home use
codes.Note: Wheelchair, fall risk, no transport. Use collapses to one room.

codes.Label: No perceived need in context
codes.Note: Rural setting, familiar route, residual vision, known house.

codes.Label: Self-reported under-use
codes.Note: I am not using them as much as I should. Said unprompted by four participants.

codes.Label: Changing vision changes the role
codes.Note: Bought with more sight. Device shifts from convenience to necessity as vision drops.

codes.Label: Existing habit wins
codes.Note: Asks the smart speaker or the search engine out of habit. The glasses never get the question.

codes.Label: Interview changed intent
codes.Note: Ends the session naming things to try. Reactivity to log in the write-up.

codes.Label: One bad experience ends it
codes.Note: A single wrong answer retires that task permanently. Needs outside proof to come back.
codes.Sub-theme: One bad experience ends the use case

codes.Label: Improves with practice
codes.Note: Learns where to point and how to ask. Competence builds if the user stays.
codes.Sub-theme: Aiming and prompting improve with practice

codes.Label: Never tried, expects failure
codes.Note: Rules the task out in advance. No failure on record.

codes.Label: Runs out of patience
codes.Note: Turns the item over and over, then gives up and reaches for another app.
codes.Sub-theme: Runs out of patience, switches tools

codes.Label: Prepares ahead
codes.Note: Studies the menu at home. Asks a friend to meet at the door.
codes.Sub-theme: Prepares ahead so the device is not needed

codes.Label: Vision varies through the day
codes.Note: Residual sight strong in the morning, weak by afternoon. Device dependence rises as the day goes on.

codes.Label: Left at home to avoid loss or damage
codes.Note: Too expensive and too fragile to wear where they might be dropped, crushed or stolen.
codes.Sub-theme: Left at home to avoid loss or damage

codes.Label: Satisfaction caps the request list
codes.Note: Happy with what it does, so never asks what else it does. Low expectations suppress demand.

codes.Label: Understood as a reader rather than an assistant
codes.Note: Treated as a one-step scanner. The AI in Meta AI is not heard as a general capability.
codes.Sub-theme: Understood as a reader rather than an assistant

codes.Label: Doing without is the baseline
codes.Note: Tasks are never attempted, so they never register as failures. The cost is invisible in any usage log.

codes.Label: Could retire a self-built labelling system
codes.Note: Braille jars and rubber bands exist because nothing read the original container.
codes.Sub-theme: Could retire a self-built labelling system

codes.Label: Came looking for a camera rather than an AI
codes.Note: Searched wearable cameras for personal safety, found these, and discovered the AI afterwards.
codes.Sub-theme: Came looking for a camera rather than an AI

codes.Label: Internalised judgement of assistive technology
codes.Note: Once thought people using text to speech were lazy, and that belief delayed adopting it.

codes.Label: Co-occurring non-visual condition shapes use
codes.Note: Attention, memory or processing conditions decide which features get used.

codes.Label: Depth perception errors
codes.Note: Mis-hit touch targets and misjudged distances, independent of acuity.

codes.Label: Blind spots determine what is missed
codes.Note: Scotoma and field loss decide which part of a scene, page or gesture never arrives.
codes.Sub-theme: Blind spots determine what is missed

codes.Label: Purchase price and comparison
codes.Note: Cross-shopped against Meta and Envision. Price a stated purchase driver.

codes.Label: Recurring fee for AI features
codes.Note: Monthly live AI fee. Accepted as fair when the feature works.

codes.Label: Generation upgrades
codes.Note: Newer generation fixes battery, speed, accuracy. Free upgrade for early buyers.

codes.Label: Long pre-order wait
codes.Note: Months between order and delivery. Shipping by order date.

codes.Label: Vendor shutdown risk
codes.Note: Blind-market vendors fold. A dead company leaves dead hardware.

codes.Label: Mainstream pricing beats blind-market pricing
codes.Note: A general-consumer device costs a fraction of purpose-built assistive hardware.

codes.Label: Price out of reach without a gift
codes.Note: Saving up for it when someone gave it. Purchase price gates access at this income level.
codes.Sub-theme: Price out of reach without a gift

codes.Label: Injury while troubleshooting
codes.Note: Fell off a treadmill fixing a dropped audio connection. Attention captured by the device.

codes.Label: Personal security outdoors
codes.Note: Hands-free means no phone held out. Less exposure, more confidence walking alone.

codes.Label: Cooking and heat risk
codes.Note: Cannot see the flame. Cannot judge doneness. Alarms set off.

codes.Label: High-stakes tasks refused or unverified
codes.Note: Device declines the risky call, or answers with no way to check it.

codes.Label: Never a mobility tool
codes.Note: Stated flatly and repeated. Crossing decisions stay with hearing and the cane.
codes.Sub-theme: Never a mobility tool, stated as doctrine

codes.Label: Checking before entering
codes.Note: Looked over a fallen fence before climbing it. Device plus volunteer as a safety check.
codes.Sub-theme: Checking a space is safe before entering

codes.Label: Crossing and traffic judgement
codes.Note: Decisions made by traffic flow and hearing. Audio output competes with that.

codes.Label: Head-level hazards
codes.Note: Branches, signs and shelves above cane height. Nothing warns about them.

codes.Label: Will not ask about the feared hazard
codes.Note: Asks for a general description rather than name the snake, the bear or the danger directly.
codes.Sub-theme: Will not ask about the feared hazard

codes.Label: Camera as evidence against a potential assailant
codes.Note: Carried so that a stranger who approaches can be photographed and identified afterwards.
codes.Sub-theme: Camera as evidence against a potential assailant

codes.Label: Silent presences and unexplained sounds
codes.Note: A quiet person in a room or an unidentified noise outdoors, with no way to resolve it.

codes.Label: Self-reported trust and satisfaction
codes.Note: Numeric ratings, with the reason attached.

codes.Label: Cites its source
codes.Note: Names the website it took the answer from. Raises trust.

codes.Label: User correction loop
codes.Note: User says that is wrong, device rechecks and revises.

codes.Label: Verification strategy
codes.Note: Prior knowledge, a sighted person, a second app, or nothing.

codes.Label: One AI checks another
codes.Note: Uses a second chatbot to verify the first.

codes.Label: Trust tiered by stakes
codes.Note: Accepts errors on trivia. Verifies on money, health, work.

codes.Label: Wrong answers delivered confidently
codes.Note: Confident errors. No confidence signal from the device.

codes.Label: Trust bounded by verifiability
codes.Note: Trusts it only where they already know the answer or the place.

codes.Label: Thin data on rare subjects
codes.Note: Obscure records, niche topics. Device has nothing to say.

codes.Label: Wants it to say it does not know
codes.Note: Hedging named as the missing feature. Silence about uncertainty is the defect.
codes.Sub-theme: Wants it to say when it does not know

codes.Label: No one to check it
codes.Note: Lives without a sighted checker. Reliability unknowable in principle.
codes.Sub-theme: No one on hand to check the answer

codes.Label: Avoids leading questions
codes.Note: Research training used as a defence. A leading question would have hidden the invention.
codes.Sub-theme: Avoids leading questions to catch fabrication

codes.Label: Blames own prompting
codes.Note: Calls it operator error. Absorbs a product problem as a personal one.
codes.Sub-theme: Blames own prompting for the failure

codes.Label: Suspected of agreeing to please
codes.Note: Is this clean. Expects a yes because a yes feels good.
codes.Sub-theme: Suspected of telling users what they want

codes.Label: Distrust learned from someone else
codes.Note: A failure seen in another user's video retires the task before a personal attempt.

codes.Label: Hallucination treated as an AI property
codes.Note: Framed as inherent to the technology rather than a bug in this product.
codes.Sub-theme: Hallucination treated as an AI property

codes.Label: Disputes the rating instrument
codes.Note: Answers the scale by questioning its wording.

codes.Label: No route to check the answer exists
codes.Note: The participant states that no method of checking is available to her.
codes.Sub-theme: No route to check the answer exists

codes.Label: Accuracy judged against no access at all
codes.Note: Better than what I had before, so an unknown error rate is acceptable.
codes.Sub-theme: Accuracy judged against no access at all

codes.Label: Cane verifies what the glasses report
codes.Note: The long cane is the instrument that confirms or refutes a spatial claim.
codes.Sub-theme: Cane verifies what the glasses report

codes.Label: Tests it on known answers
codes.Note: Deliberately asks about things already known by touch, to gauge how far it can be trusted.

codes.Label: Says the information is absent when present
codes.Note: Reports no expiration date, no chair, nothing there, when the thing is there.
codes.Sub-theme: Says the information is absent when present

codes.Label: Attributes a limit to a policy rule
codes.Note: Reads a capability failure as a legal or liability restriction, and accepts it on that basis.
codes.Sub-theme: Attributes a limit to a policy rule

codes.Label: Rates generously and says so
codes.Note: Names the tendency to give high scores while giving one. A caution on every rating in the set.

codes.Label: Uses AI to screen for scams
codes.Note: Screenshots an advert or an email and asks a general AI whether it is legitimate.
codes.Sub-theme: Uses AI to screen for scams

codes.Label: Finding an address
codes.Note: Names the number and street. Gets to the area, not the door.

codes.Label: Walking directions
codes.Note: Tested on known routes only. Street noise buries the answer.

codes.Label: Open-ended exploration
codes.Note: Live mode at a park or festival. Head turned slowly to sweep the scene.

codes.Label: Indoor layout and exits
codes.Note: Room contents described well. Find me the exit, refused or failed.

codes.Label: Ruled out for travel
codes.Note: Not experimented with, or barred on principle. Cane, dog, and hearing keep the job.

codes.Label: Nearby places wrong
codes.Note: Knows the street address, then names a bus stop seven blocks off and a cinema five miles away.

codes.Label: Reads signs in place
codes.Note: Building signs after an Uber drop. Sale signs through glass. Museum placards.

codes.Label: Transit stops and stations
codes.Note: Which station is next, which platform, where the door is.

codes.Label: Detours and wrong turns
codes.Note: Construction, closures, a driver who dropped them in the wrong place.

codes.Label: Obstacle checking on a route
codes.Note: Asked for on a changed or unfamiliar stretch, not continuously.

codes.Label: Finding an unoccupied seat
codes.Note: Pews, buses, waiting rooms. Currently solved by tapping a cane against strangers' feet.

codes.Label: Identifying the right rideshare vehicle
codes.Note: Colour, make and plate against a line of waiting cars. Named by three participants.

codes.Label: Directions in body-relative units
codes.Note: Wants left, right and distance in feet from the body rather than it is right there.

codes.Label: Cognitive load of collision avoidance
codes.Note: Crowded stations consume the attention that would otherwise operate the device.

codes.Label: Aiming by head
codes.Note: Head as the tripod. Residual vision or a guess. Panning to keep a moving subject in frame.

codes.Label: Assistive audio in the take
codes.Note: Screen reader audible on the finished video. Rules out the phone as the camera.
codes.Sub-theme: Assistive audio lands in the recording

codes.Label: Clip names unusable
codes.Note: Identical generated names, wrong order in the editor. Renames every clip by hand.

codes.Label: No framing check
codes.Note: Nothing confirms the subject is in shot. Wants coaching or a check, mostly has not thought to ask.
codes.Sub-theme: No framing check before or after

codes.Label: Point of view capture
codes.Note: Short clips for social platforms. The reason the glasses were bought.
codes.Sub-theme: Point of view capture as the primary use

codes.Label: Editing and publishing
codes.Note: Chatbot writes the caption and reformats per platform. Glasses do capture only.

codes.Label: Cannot tell if recording
codes.Note: Tones too alike. Clips that never appeared. Talking to nothing.
codes.Sub-theme: Cannot tell if it is recording

codes.Label: Voice sending to contacts
codes.Note: Take it and send it, no phone. Named as a favourite feature.

codes.Label: Cannot send a capture without the phone
codes.Note: The glasses take the photo and then hand the user back to a screen they cannot use.
codes.Sub-theme: Cannot send a capture without the phone

codes.Label: Glasses used as the microphone
codes.Note: The microphone, not the camera, is the reason to wear them for a recording.

codes.Label: Recorded audio cuts in and out
codes.Note: Music or capture drops mid-take, cause unclear to the wearer.
codes.Sub-theme: Recorded audio cuts in and out

codes.Label: Professional documents
codes.Note: Agendas, biographies, brokerage letters, PDFs, cover letters.
codes.Sub-theme: Board papers, agendas and professional documents

codes.Label: Works in the field
codes.Note: Judges the device professionally. Cites published reports and hospital deployments.

codes.Label: Automated interview checks
codes.Note: Recorded interview, nobody to ask. AI checks how the frame looks.

codes.Label: Job tasks on the glasses
codes.Note: Product inventory, shade codes on the base of a lipstick, catalogue pages.
codes.Sub-theme: Job tasks handed to the glasses

codes.Label: Employer clock wins
codes.Note: A task owed on time. Retry budget runs out before the read succeeds.

codes.Label: Work designed around the gap
codes.Note: The job is shaped so the visual task never has to happen.

codes.Label: Unpaid accessibility testing
codes.Note: Testing products for companies without pay, as the route into the field.

codes.Label: Buys by readability
codes.Note: Left a bank over its app. Replaced a stove for contrast. Bought the simplest dishwasher.
codes.Sub-theme: Buys banks, apps and appliances by readability

codes.Label: Venue lighting too dark
codes.Note: Restaurants dark by design. Flashlight carried as the fix.
codes.Sub-theme: Venue lighting too dark to read

codes.Label: Light fonts and low contrast
codes.Note: White on pink, grey on white, etched steel. Sighted people struggle too.
codes.Sub-theme: Light fonts and low contrast print

codes.Label: Appliance panels unreadable
codes.Note: Fifty options on a flush panel. White on white. App control or a new appliance instead.

codes.Label: QR codes to unreadable pages
codes.Note: Scan works, destination is a light-font page that pixelates on zoom.
codes.Sub-theme: QR codes leading to unreadable pages

codes.Label: Screen unusable outdoors
codes.Note: Daylight wipes the display. Glasses become the only viable camera outside.

codes.Label: Text inside images
codes.Note: Catalogues pack copy into pictures to save space. Nothing to parse cleanly.

codes.Label: Unlabeled controls
codes.Note: Screen reader announces button, button, button. Which one is anyone's guess.

codes.Label: Kiosks, card readers and ticket machines
codes.Note: Touchscreens in the world with no non-visual path. Named as the single largest barrier.
codes.Sub-theme: Kiosks, card readers and ticket machines

codes.Label: The world is not laid out to be read
codes.Note: Cues placed where no camera can pick them up. Buttons on some placards and not others.
codes.Sub-theme: The world is not laid out to be read

codes.Label: User preconditions the environment
codes.Note: Raises screen contrast, cleans the glass, moves to a window, flips the box, so the device can succeed.

codes.Label: Accessibility information flows one way
codes.Note: A rideshare app tells the rider the driver is hearing impaired, and tells the driver nothing.

codes.Label: Continuous description in use
codes.Note: An always-on mode running while walking or exploring.

codes.Label: Wants to choose what gets described
codes.Note: A checklist: scenery, buildings, people, hazards. Not everything.
codes.Sub-theme: Wants to choose what gets described

codes.Label: Narration talks over the conversation
codes.Note: Keeps describing while the user is speaking to a person.

codes.Label: No quick pause or gesture
codes.Note: No way to stop the stream without ending the session.

codes.Label: Speech rate too slow
codes.Note: Screen reader users want it faster than the maximum on offer.

codes.Label: Wants the important thing first
codes.Note: Starbucks, a person in front, a step. Not every sign on the street.

codes.Label: Continuous mode changes the voice
codes.Note: The live voice is echoing and tunnel-like, and masks natural hearing. Named as the reason it is off.

codes.Label: Listening effort and speech rate
codes.Note: Audio-only output is work. Speech too fast to process is as unusable as print too small to read.

codes.Label: Volunteer guides a physical task
codes.Note: A person on the call steering a hand to a button, a bottle label, an egg.

codes.Label: Connect time defeats the task
codes.Note: By the time the call lands the moment has passed.

codes.Label: Nobody picks up
codes.Note: Rings for minutes. Sometimes no volunteer at all.

codes.Label: Helper cannot see well enough
codes.Note: The volunteer asks for the phone instead, or cannot read the panel.

codes.Label: Human preferred over the AI
codes.Note: The volunteer route chosen deliberately over the on-board assistant.

codes.Label: Taste and judgement reserved for a human
codes.Note: Matching tissue paper to a gift bag is described as needing a human element rather than an answer.
codes.Sub-theme: Taste and judgement reserved for a human

codes.Label: Battery capacity falls with age
codes.Note: The same device does less each year. Directly named as a reason for lower use.

codes.Label: Battery cannot be replaced
codes.Note: No access to the cell, so a dead battery ends the device.

codes.Label: Aftermarket battery add-ons
codes.Note: Magnetic packs clipped to the arm. Longer runtime, more weight.

codes.Label: Owning more than one pair
codes.Note: A second pair as the workaround for runtime and failure.

codes.Label: Phone must stay within range
codes.Note: The glasses stop working once the host phone is out of range, and the stated range is not the working range.

codes.Label: Locating the glasses themselves
codes.Note: No way to make the glasses sound off when they are put down and lost.
